1. SURFACE: log line = ISO8601 UTC timestamp + level tag (INFO/ERROR/WARN, padded) + msg + key=val fields. Plain ASCII, space-delim, syslog-ish app log dialect.

2. CONTENT: Match surface. No mismatch — timestamps consistent, levels consistent, structure consistent.

CONTENT VERDICT: NO MISMATCH

3. MISREADINGS:
- Grep `ERROR` substring matches other lines containing word "ERROR" inside msg/fields of non-ERROR lines (e.g. INFO line describing an error). Evidence: none in sample, but risk exists — must anchor match to level field position (start-of-line token after timestamp), not free substring search.
- Level field width varies (`INFO ` two spaces vs `WARN` one space vs `ERROR` one space) — naive fixed-column parse could misalign. Evidence: sample shows `INFO  ` (2sp), `ERROR ` (1sp), `WARN ` (1sp) — padding is to align column, not fixed width, so split-on-whitespace safe, fixed-substring unsafe.
- Case sensitivity: matching lowercase "error" won't catch — log uses uppercase only. Evidence: all samples uppercase.
- Multi-line stack traces (not shown in sample) could cause continuation lines miscounted as separate entries or ERROR block undercounted if grep counts only first line. Can't confirm/deny from 8-line sample — flag as unchecked risk given 5210 total lines.
